quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes on a multilane highway?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert drivers that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning sign.

questions.question: What happens when driving on gravel or dirt roads?

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Loose gravel and dirt do not give your tires as much grip as concrete or asphalt. You must slow down on these surfaces. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: Is failing to look both ways behind the car the most common backing mistake?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The most common backing mistake is not looking both ways behind the car. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to the right and look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: What should you do before driving after taking any medicine?

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive more slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about any medicine before driving. This is especially important for tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about conditions on or near the road.
It helps direct you to cities and towns ahead.
It tells you about traffic laws and regulations.
It tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about conditions on or near the road ahead. They are diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for road conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always follow speed limits and slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Does higher speed mean longer stopping distance when reacting to other drivers?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: The faster you are driving, the longer it takes to stop when you need to react to other drivers' unexpected actions.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: Both effects may be increased.
Nothing will happen.
Both effects may be reduced.
Only the alcohol effect may be reduced.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both effects may be increased.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, having one drink while taking a cold medicine could affect you like having several drinks.

questions.question: What is important to remember about trucks on the road?

options.text: They need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
They need less time to pass going downhill than smaller vehicles.
They have a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
They need less time to pass going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because of their size, trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: You must always give them the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to give them the right-of-way at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always give the right-of-way to someone using a guide dog or carrying a white cane.

questions.question: When a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Pull over to the right side of the road.
Stop your vehicle as far away from traffic as possible.
Turn off your engine, radio, and other devices that may block your hearing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop as far from traffic as possible. Turn off your engine, radio, and other devices so you can hear the officer.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings if they obey traffic signals. Vehicles must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, whether marked or unmarked.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to get rid of the alcohol naturally.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to get rid of the alcohol naturally.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC. They may keep you awake, but they will not make you sober.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?

options.text: During the night.
During the day.
Only under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions. It is safest to drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the limit. All drivers must maintain a safe speed at all times.

questions.question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop at an intersection.
When there is a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a red traffic light. Always obey directions from police officers directing traffic, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther back from other vehicles.
Approach all vehicles with caution.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear in snow. Increase your distance from other vehicles because slippery roads need more distance to stop.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden, unsafe lane changes.
They have many passengers in their car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden, unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for aggressive drivers who make sudden, unsafe lane changes. Do not challenge them. The safest thing to do is get out of their way.

questions.question: When a truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right, what should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus moves.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning first.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning first.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve.
Winding road ahead.
Pavement ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has many curves and turns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are making a turn.
You have your emergency brake on.
You are changing lanes.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working properly at all times.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: What happens when you tailgate (drive too close to another car's rear bumper)?

options.text: It can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
You cannot get a traffic ticket for it.
It prevents being cut off and reduces accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous and can lead to aggressive driving. You can face legal consequences for unsafe driving.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on the interstate?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and go back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and go back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines divide the road, is passing allowed?

options.text: Yes, from the left.
Yes, from the right.
No, not from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, not from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean that cars going in both directions cannot cross the center line to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, should you pull to the right and wait for it to pass?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches, pull to the right side of the road immediately and let it pass.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: They make turning more difficult.
They increase the chance of hydroplaning.
They increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Keep your tires properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread and proper air pressure. Slow down when driving in the rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: When a stop line is present at a stop sign, where must you stop?

options.text: At the line.
On top of the line.
Only if pedestrians are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the line.
questions.explanation: You must stop before the stop line or crosswalk. Proceed when it is safe to do so.
